        This amendment enables your company to convert the share premium reserve into Class B shares of URW N.V.

      • Terms:
        At the exercise of such conversion, your Company shall subscribe for the Class B shares at the Exercise Price of EUR 0.50 for each Class B share, or
        for such other price as may be agreed between your Company and URW N.V.
        The Exercise Price shall not be less than the nominal value of one Class B share.

      • Reason justifying the interest of the agreement:
        This amendment was concluded to guarantee your Company the discretionary right to convert the share premium reserve into URW N.V. Class B
        shares and thus to secure the amount of the capitalized loans.

  Given the ongoing geopolitical and macro-economic conditions, including the threat of deepening trade wars and customs barriers, sovereign
  debt concerns and potential recession in Europe, URW continues to monitor and anticipate the evolving impacts on the business, particularly
  concerning interest rates, inflation, supply chain issues, regulatory and tax changes. In addition, growing social and political instability in some
  countries where the Group operates - which includes the increasing threat posed by Russian expansionism to regional stability in Europe, which
  could degenerate into broader conflict - may significantly affect consumption, security, financing, capital markets and investor appetite.

  In light of the uncertain evolution of the international geopolitical situation arising from the armed conflict in the Middle East, the Group’s risk
  mapping and/or the assessment of those risks may deteriorate rapidly due to major economic, financial and social impacts — whether identified
  or not — stemming from the conflict or from any potential escalation. Such impacts could have a potentially significant adverse effect on the
  Group’s activities, budget assumptions, financial forecasts, and announced strategy.


6.2.1 Ratings of the main specific risk factors
The Group risk inventory, used for Group risk mapping, is composed of 11 Group-specific risks organised into 5 categories. The risks presented below
are rated within each category in descending order of impact on the Group (first ones being the most impactful) and likelihood.

This rating is based on:
(i) The potential net impact corresponding to the potential (financial/legal/reputational) impact after risk management measures have been put in
     place (net impact); and
(ii) The potential net likelihood of the risk event, after risk management measures have been put in place (net likelihood).
This rating is the result of the Group management assessment performed under the ERM framework described in section 6.1.2 Group Enterprise Risk
Management framework of this 2025 Universal Registration Document and depends on the subjective assessments of management.

The risk rating criteria for net impact and net likelihood are regularly reviewed by the GRC in line with the Group’s circumstances and evolving risk
appetite. Legend used below:

      pandemics (previously included in Health and Safety). The revised risk factor places significant emphasis on crisis management and business
      continuity planning.


      6.2.2 Detailed main risk factors
      6.2.2.1 Category #1: Business sector and operational risks
      Investment and divestment
      Part of URW’s core business model is value creation through investment in and divestment of assets. The profitability of these transactions depends
      on the accuracy of initial financial assumptions, market conditions (including available financing and investors’ appetite), tax environment, quality and
      attractiveness of assets, and legal and regulatory considerations. Improper investment and divestment strategy/decisions could have an adverse
      impact on asset performance, brand reputation and growth prospects. For indicative sensitivity regarding the evolution of URW’s shopping centre
      asset values, please refer to Chapter 4, section 4.1.3.

      The Group remains cautious about the ever-evolving macroeconomic environment. A rise in inflation and interest rates could impact investor appetite
      and capital markets, potentially hindering the Group’s ability to deliver its capital allocation strategy.

      Main risk factors                                                  Main risk management measures
      • Inappropriate capital allocation strategy, decisions and         • Group decision-making process that actively involves both the MB and SB for major projects

      • Improper asset valuations/inaccurate financial performance       • Dedicated approval process for proposed transactions;
        forecast.                                                        • Thresholds set and agreed by MB/SB (CAPEX, returns targets on acquisitions, yield on cost for
                                                                           development projects etc.);
                                                                         • Recurring strategic review of capital allocation decisions between the MB and SB to ensure full
                                                                           alignment with Group targets;
                                                                         • Strategic mapping of the Group’s portfolio with asset-by-asset action plan/roadmap; and
                                                                         • Regular market analysis to understand current trends and market dynamics.
